name: Princess Purse
blurb: A dated, cluttered storefront rebuilt around the product photography — a calmer palette, real hierarchy in the navigation, and a hero that finally sells the bags instead of competing with them.
summary: Replaced the crowded three-row header with a single clean bar — logo, search, account, cart.
Rebuilt the hero around the product photography instead of a stock image with text stacked on top.
Cut the navigation down to real categories, so buyers reach a product in fewer clicks.
Made the whole storefront properly responsive — the old one was barely usable on a phone.

name: Madrona Recovery
blurb: Families arrive here in a crisis, so the rebuild is about clarity under stress — a warmer, more confident identity and a path that gets parents to the right program without hunting for it.
summary: Put the primary actions — Referral, Client Portal, Call Now — in the header where a parent in a crisis can find them.
Rebuilt the program structure so families land on the right level of care instead of browsing.
Warmer, more confident visual identity while keeping the calm the subject demands.
Accessible contrast and type sizing throughout — this audience is not reading on a good day.

name: Component Supply
blurb: Hypotubes, mandrels, PTFE, heat shrink — a deep technical catalog for medical device engineers who arrive knowing the exact part number they need. The redesign is built around getting them to it.
summary: Rebuilt the catalog navigation around how engineers actually search — by spec, not by marketing category.
Cleaner product presentation so a highly technical catalog stops reading like a spreadsheet.
Modern, mobile-responsive storefront on the current cart version.
Kept the URL structure intact through the rebuild so existing search rankings survived.

name: Booth Filter Store
blurb: A deep, technical catalog where customers know exactly what they need and just have to find it. The redesign puts findability first — clearer merchandising, and a storefront that holds up on a phone in a workshop.
summary: Findability first: search and category structure surfaced, because these buyers arrive knowing the part they need.
Cleaner product merchandising so a technical catalog stops looking like a spreadsheet.
Rebuilt mobile layout — the store gets used on a phone, on a shop floor, in gloves.
Hand-coded on the PinnacleCart platform, no page-builder bloat.

name: PRO Scientific
blurb: A US manufacturer of rotor-stator and multi-sample homogenizers for biotech, pharma, and food science. The rebuild gives serious lab equipment a storefront that looks as precise as the instruments.
summary: Rebuilt the product presentation to match the precision of the instruments being sold.
Clearer paths by application — biotech, pharma, food, cosmetics — rather than one flat catalog.
Modern responsive storefront on the current cart version.
Kept the technical depth buyers need while cutting the visual clutter around it.

name: Hollywood Poster Frames
blurb: A wholesale frame supplier with a catalog spanning movie posters, comics, albums, and certificates — every size, every format. The redesign makes a sprawling catalog navigable.
summary: Restructured a sprawling catalog so buyers can find a frame by size and format, not by scrolling.
Modernized the storefront and brought it onto a current, mobile-responsive theme.
Cleaner product imagery — the product is a frame, so the presentation has to get out of its way.
Rebuilt the checkout path for wholesale buyers ordering in volume.

name: Velodrome Shop
blurb: A specialist track-cycling store rebuilt for an audience that knows exactly what it wants — clean product presentation and a storefront that doesn't get in the way of the bike.
summary: Rebuilt the storefront around the product photography.
Simplified the navigation for a specialist audience that shops by category and spec.
Modern, mobile-responsive layout on a current theme.
Cleaner, faster front end than the template it replaced.

name: The Monster Makers
blurb: Latex, foam, clay and mold-making supplies for prop and creature builders. A cult catalog that deserved a storefront with as much character as the work it supplies.
summary: Rebuilt the storefront to match the character of the craft it serves.
Restructured the catalog by material and process, the way a builder actually shops.
Modern, mobile-responsive layout on the current cart version.
Delivered on a staging sandbox for review before go-live.

name: Oxman & Oxman
blurb: A full-service Colorado law firm. People arriving here are usually having a bad week — so the rebuild is about credibility, clarity, and making it obvious how to reach a human.
summary: Rebuilt around trust signals — the practice areas and the attorneys, not stock imagery.
Made contact unmissable: a prospective client should never hunt for the phone number.
Clear practice-area structure so visitors self-select into the right matter fast.
Modern, mobile-responsive rebuild — most people find a lawyer on a phone.

name: Thunderbolt Group
blurb: The agency's own site — the hardest client. Traded a stock-photo skyline and a slow preloader for a sharper, faster brand presence that actually shows the work.
summary: Killed the full-screen preloader that made the old site feel broken before it even appeared.
Dropped the stock skyline hero for a layout that actually shows the agency's work and clients.
Rebuilt the page structure so services and case studies are reachable, not buried.
Faster load and a sharper brand presence — the site an agency should be able to point at.

name: Phoenix Enterprises (PE)
blurb: Connectors, IC sockets, ribbon cable, hook-up wire — a long-established components supplier running on a legacy cart and an aging theme. Migrated to the current cart version and re-themed, live, without losing the catalog.
summary: Upgraded the store to the latest cart version.
Replaced the legacy theme with a current, mobile-responsive template.
Migrated a large components catalog intact — products, categories, and customer accounts.
Kept the store trading throughout; no downtime, no lost URLs.

name: BuyMerchant
blurb: Bulk closeouts and wholesale lots for nonprofits, charities, and promotional buyers. Brought off a dated theme and an old cart build onto the current version.
summary: Upgraded the store to the latest cart version.
Re-themed onto a current, mobile-responsive template.
Preserved the catalog, pricing tiers, and customer accounts through the migration.
Cleaner bulk-buying paths for the wholesale and nonprofit audience.

name: Horse Smarts
blurb: Equestrian jewelry, engraved awards, and breed-specific designs — a gift catalog where people arrive shopping for a horse, a Corgi, a Doberman. The redesign is built around letting them browse by the thing they love.
summary: Rebuilt the catalog around how people actually shop it — by breed and by occasion, not by product type.
Gave the jewelry and engraved pieces the product photography they deserved instead of a cramped grid.
Modern, mobile-responsive storefront — gift shopping happens on a phone.
Clearer path from browsing a design to ordering it engraved.

name: DuraReady
blurb: No-fade, chemical-resistant labels for Zebra and DYMO printers — a highly technical SKU catalog where the right label is a spec, not a style. Upgraded and re-themed.
summary: Upgraded the store to the latest cart version.
Re-themed onto a current, mobile-responsive template.
Kept the spec-driven catalog navigable — buyers choose by material, size, and resistance.
Delivered alongside the live store so it could be reviewed before switching over.

name: 7 Day Drapes
blurb: A new storefront, built from nothing. Quick-ship custom drapery, made in the USA — a configurable product sold online, which means the hard part is making a made-to-measure purchase feel simple.
summary: Built from scratch — no previous site to rebuild from.
Designed the buying flow around a made-to-measure product: fabric, pleat, size, lining.
Mobile-first storefront; most drapery shopping starts on a phone.
Hand-coded front end on the PinnacleCart platform.

name: Component Supply — Blog
blurb: A new editorial section for a medical-device component supplier — built so their engineering content has a home that supports the catalog rather than sitting apart from it.
summary: New blog section built from scratch, matched to the storefront it lives inside.
Readable long-form layout for genuinely technical content.
Built to support the catalog — content that leads back to the parts it discusses.
Responsive and hand-coded, consistent with the main store.

name: Bevel Heaven
blurb: Bevel-drive Ducati spares — Dellorto, Brembo, Ceriani, Marzocchi — for restorers keeping 1970s machines on the road. Distributing worldwide since 2002, but running on a cart and theme that had aged out from under them.
summary: Upgraded the store to the latest cart version.
Re-themed onto a current, mobile-responsive template — the old one was a fixed-width, desktop-only layout.
Migrated a deep parts catalog intact, right down to the model-specific fitment categories restorers navigate by.
Kept the store trading through the migration: same products, same customers, same URLs.
